scope: Every tracked Go file and package under agentplane, including tests, generated tracked files, fixtures, commands and experiments. All top-level Agentplane areas remain visible as context. This is a target-organization proposal, not a claim that proposed APIs or directories are implemented.

legend.~: Deferred authentication or protobuf contract decision

structure_rules: Sequence by certainty: delete leftovers first, then layout fixes that hold under any service map, then moves that follow agreed service directions, then extractions behind a local contract, and last the moves that wait on an open service decision. Move or rename each file once: when an agreed or open boundary change would move a file again, its in-component move waits for that change.

Use current vocabulary in every new or moved name. The Environment Runtime is not a runner. A Journal is what a harness or process emits, stored verbatim; a Thread is the messaging object with editable messages, so no new code names the folded projection a Thread. Wire, stored and security names change only through their own migration.

Organize by executable authority and domain responsibility. Keep APIs, private implementations, persistence, tests and composition discoverable under their owning component; do not add language-specific go/ directories.

Use cmd/ for service composition and maintenance entry points. Move a whole command package first where needed; extract real behavior from main under a named private owner rather than merely hiding the same package under cmd/.

A directory and its package name should describe the same responsibility. Record intentional exceptions for generated packages, external-test packages and useful import disambiguation; eliminate leftover pre-move names and redundant owner prefixes.

Use internal/ for implementation visibility. A second internal/ is useful only when it enforces a narrower real owner; nesting alone is not a goal. Keep public contracts and deliberate cross-service test fixtures outside the restricted subtree.

Split concrete state owners, adapters or pure behavior, not arbitrary file batches. File count and LOC identify review candidates but are not a package-size rule. A shared transaction or lifecycle fence needs an explicit ownership contract before extraction.

One owner controls begin/commit/rollback, generation/incarnation fences, admission, cancellation, drain and joins for its operation. Leaves receive narrow immutable inputs or an explicitly caller-owned transaction; never pass a whole mutable service aggregate merely to relocate methods.

Provider-specific interpretation, selectors, native data and projection belong beside that provider. Generic inbox, transport or scheduling code consumes typed boundary inputs; avoid any-based registries or plugin frameworks to facilitate moves.

Keep tests beside the behavior they assert. Cross-service scenarios use intentional testing contracts. Preserve publication, rollback, recovery, security and no-replay coverage when splitting fixtures.

Preserve wire names, stored representations and deployed executable/image contracts during ordinary organization changes. Authentication/SPIFFE choices and protobuf namespace alignment remain separately deferred designs.

Target 200–3,000 changed LOC per coherent PR after rename detection, including all imports, BUILD, CI/release, runfiles, manifests and docs consumers. Do not add filler; split larger work by concrete responsibility. Use native GitHub Stacks for actual content dependencies.

On merge, delete the landed work item, exact mappings and dependencies; refresh the immutable current inventory and revisit affected package decisions. Keep only remaining work in the plan. A new package or unclassified file requires review before coverage is claimed.

target_binaries.proposal_quote: So, what's the plan on how we will structure binaries? One binary that handles sandbox controller kubernetes stuff and also communicates with the env runtimes in those sandboxes for running commands and starting native sessions in hosted harnesses and codex exec server stuff? And a separate binary handles the routing of commands to *sessions*, which would go either to central sampler or to hosted harnesses through the first binary?
target_binaries.summary: Two binaries replace `runner-gateway` and `sandbox-controller`. The Environments binary owns Sandboxes and everything that calls an Environment Runtime; the Sessions binary owns Session admission, the durable command queue and routing, and reaches Runtimes only through the Environments binary. The Runner Gateway disappears. After gateway-connection-lease-removal its Runtime proxy and Executor keep no per-Sandbox state, and the Dispatcher already calls the proxy over the network (`dispatcher/runner_client.go` dials the per-Sandbox control Service even inside its own Pod), so moving the proxy out adds no hop. Before this direction the plan, and the merge contract drafted in #16311 (closed as superseded), kept the Gateway as Dispatcher plus proxy.

cut_line.title: Runtime calls from the Sessions binary
cut_line.today: The Dispatcher's `ProxyRunner` already calls the proxy over gRPC. The proxy admits `CreateSession`, `SubmitInput`, `ChangeModel`, `ChangeReasoningEffort` and `InterruptTurn` only from the combined Gateway/Dispatcher account, proven at startup to belong to the serving Pod (`dispatcherAccount`).
cut_line.proposal: The Environments proxy grants those methods to the Sessions binary's workload identity instead, and callers address the Environments Service. After gateway-connection-lease-removal; receivers before senders.

cut_line.title: Automatic wake and its budget
cut_line.decision: Operator, 2026-11-14 05:19 UTC, card "Choose which binary performs automatic wakes after the split": "Sessions binary wakes".
cut_line.today: The delivery worker calls `lifecycle.Manager.RequestWake` in process. It checks `wakeOnSend`, the Identity's `resumePolicy.allowOwnServiceAccount` or the `wake_callers` broker grant, refuses after a requested stop, reserves the budget (10 distinct wake generations per effective caller per 60 s) in the Dispatcher's PostgreSQL and patches `spec.running` and `spec.wakeGeneration`.
cut_line.proposal: The Sessions binary keeps that policy check and the budget and writes the Sandbox spec itself, so nothing calls across for a wake and the Environments binary needs no budget call back (the controller-only budget RPC in #16318 is closed). The automatic path of `lifecycle` stays with the Dispatcher and explicit resume moves with EnvironmentService. `sandbox_controller/internal` is not importable from the Dispatcher, so split `lifecycle` along that line or keep the shared policy outside both `internal/` trees.

cut_line.title: Rate bound for explicit resume
cut_line.today: `ResumeEnvironment` spends the same budget, but only direct Pod-bound `operator_callers` can resume today (`eligibilityFor`). The environment-rule work adds Identity callers.
cut_line.proposal: Operators need no budget. Decide the Environments-side bound when Identity callers arrive; the Environments binary has no database for one.

cut_line.title: Identity change against Session admission
cut_line.today: `SetEnvironmentIdentity` patches the Sandbox inside `dispatcher.Store.ChangeSandboxIdentity`, holding the per-Sandbox advisory lock Session admission takes, and refuses while Sessions name another Identity.
cut_line.proposal: Carried from #16311. Either (a) Environments authenticates the caller, resolves the Identity's exact UID and calls a private Sessions operation with the Sandbox UID, expected resource version and desired Identity, which Sessions re-reads and patches under its exclusive lock; the lock alone is no fence, because cancellation, a lost connection or process death can release it while the patch may still commit, so a durable pending identity-change record that admission checks stays until reconciliation shows the resulting binding. This is the one remaining Environments-to-Sessions call. Or (b) no call: Sessions re-checks the live Identity at admission and before delivery (delivery's `executionCurrent` already does) and Environments patches under optimistic locking. Either way a same-name replacement, a conflict, a failed query or an unavailable peer never becomes an unguarded mutation.

cut_line.title: The Sessions binary's view of Sandboxes
cut_line.today: The delivery worker and admission read Sandboxes through `internal/sandboxinventory` (the Dispatcher's catalog over the process's informer cache of Sandboxes, Pods and VMs) plus an uncached Identity reader. The proxy reads the same informer cache directly.
cut_line.proposal: `internal/sandboxinventory` stays with the Sessions binary over its own read-only Kubernetes cache, so delivery adds no call; the proxy reads the Environments binary's cache.

cut_line.title: Every-replica serving in the Environments binary
cut_line.today: The Sandbox Controller is a leader-elected manager with no listener.
cut_line.proposal: Carried from #16311. The gRPC server (EnvironmentService, proxy, Executor) gets its own non-leader-elected lifecycle, readiness, TLS identity, audience, TokenReview/SVID and delegation settings, Service and projected credentials. Readiness means the listener and its dependencies work and never waits for leadership. Shutdown stops accepting, drains streams and joins serving work without holding up reconciliation handoff. Watches and live reads keep today's freshness and stream re-authorization.

cut_line.title: Rollout order
cut_line.today: One binary serves every caller today.
cut_line.proposal: Carried from #16311. Receivers before senders; settings in code before manifests set them. Deploy the Environments serving path behind an unused Service and exercise auth, readiness and multi-replica behaviour with the app unavailable; then retarget callers (destination audiences, credentials, cdk8s, RBAC, the system overview diagram). Remove old wiring only after traffic has left and the last safe rollback image and config pair is recorded, and never combine an RBAC removal with a deployment that still needs the grant. Acceptance: identity change raced against admission in both orders, explicit and automatic wake from different replicas, non-leader serving and leader handoff, and a mixed-version rollout and rollback.

keep_alive.steer: Operator, 2026-11-14 05:18 UTC: something like "please keep this sandbox alive for me until time X" would be probably reasonable; the design is left to us.
keep_alive.today: Only the Runtime extends awake time. It clears `idle-since` while any Session has an active turn, pending input or a running setup, while an admission or an Executor call or session is open, and during bootstrap. The controller starts its timer when it first sees an `idle-since` and, at `spec.idleSuspendAfter`, asks the Runtime to quiesce only if it is still idle since that instant; the Runtime refuses if anything arrived in between, and a controller restart starts every timer over. Nothing outside the Sandbox extends awake time. Queued commands do not need to: a running Sandbox gets them delivered at once, which makes the Runtime busy. A central Session's executor environment is never woken: the Dispatcher skips its readiness and wake on purpose, and the sampler retries `Unavailable` until its deadline.
proposal: A hold is one record per Sandbox and holder principal, with an absolute expiry. Renewing replaces the holder's own record; releasing deletes it. Holders hold a Sandbox, not a Session, so no per-Session record reaches control-plane storage.
The effective hold is the latest unexpired expiry across holders. While it is in the future the controller starts no idle suspend and reports the hold and its holders on the Sandbox's status.
Holds never wake. Waking stays with the Sessions binary (automatic) and operators (explicit resume): a requester that needs a suspended Sandbox wakes it, then holds it.

A requested stop wins. Holds never keep running, or bring back, a Sandbox someone stopped; a hold request on a stopped or quiescing Sandbox is refused with the Sandbox's state, as a wake assessment is today.

Expiry only suspends. When the last hold lapses the ordinary idle rule applies again, timed from the later of the lapse and the Runtime's `idle-since`; a lapse never quiesces, deletes or stops anything itself.

Event-driven. The controller watches hold records and re-evaluates the Sandbox on every change, and schedules its next evaluation at the effective expiry, a known deadline like today's idle timer. Nothing polls.

Authority. Holding a running Sandbox is weaker than resuming it, so whoever may resume a Sandbox may hold it: operators, its Identity under `resumePolicy` or the environment rule's resume operation, and configured wake brokers. The central sampler may hold the exact executor environment named in a central Session it runs. A configured maximum hold length bounds each request.

First holders: the central sampler holds its executor environment while a turn runs, model time between tool calls included; people hold from the app or CLI ("until 18:00"). Sessions delivery needs none.

Storage: Kubernetes Lease objects, one per Sandbox and holder, owned by the Sandbox so deletion removes them and written only by the Environments binary after authorization. Durable and watchable without a database for the Environments binary; writes happen per request or renewal, never per command.

Central executor wake: following the card, the Sessions binary wakes a central Session's executor environment when it delivers input to that Session, still delivering to the sampler without waiting for Ready, and the sampler then holds it.

questions.text: Name the two binaries' directories. The Sessions binary leaves `runner_gateway/` (proposal: `session_dispatcher/`, matching the `SessionDispatcher` service and its SVID); the Environments binary keeps `sandbox_controller/` or becomes `environments/` beside its API. The Sessions command and assembly wait on this so their files move once.

package_decisions.role: Egress proxy composition and service command

package_decisions.gate: Preserve executable and image contracts.

package_decisions.role: Embedded CLI guide content
package_decisions.reason: The CLI imports this package to embed the egress operator and workload guides; content ownership follows the CLI contract.
package_decisions.gate: Keep docs embedding and CLI callers together.

package_decisions.role: Admin and health RPC implementation
package_decisions.reason: This owns administrative history reads/change watch and health; cmd composes it, while workload-facing EgressRules has a separate authorization boundary.
package_decisions.gate: Keep method-level authorization and admin/workload separation.

package_decisions.role: Egress admission vocabulary and persisted/logged record
package_decisions.reason: Six production packages share the same admission outcome and record; history, proxy, policy and admin need one vocabulary, not local copies.
package_decisions.gate: Preserve event metadata and the rule that records contain no secret values or paths.

package_decisions.role: Egress decision history store and query
package_decisions.reason: The proxy writes decisions and admin serves them; both are egress-owned behavior over the shared PostgreSQL primitives.
package_decisions.gate: Keep egress schema and logical history ownership service-local.

package_decisions.role: Embedded egress history schema
package_decisions.reason: The serving binary embeds this service-owned Goose schema; nesting makes the schema ownership explicit.
package_decisions.gate: Do not move egress schema into shared postgres/migrate.

package_decisions.role: Egress workload SVID admission adapter
package_decisions.reason: The proxy and sidecar use this egress-specific live credential decision, while generic TLS verification and credential resolution remain in net/peertls and identity.
package_decisions.gate: Defer authentication/SPIFFE mechanism choices; do not merge authorization or delegation roles.

package_decisions.role: Egress credential and Secret informer adapter
package_decisions.reason: This single production source combines the egress-only generated credential/Secret watches with policy reader data; its single-file size reflects one adapter, not a shared generic informer API.
package_decisions.gate: Keep egress credential/Secret watches with egress; Policy Reader remains shared.

package_decisions.role: In-memory egress policy evaluation
package_decisions.reason: This owns effective rule selection and decision evaluation; it consumes the shared policy index and egress resource parser, and is used by proxy, rules and admin.
package_decisions.gate: Keep pure evaluation separate from API watches and HTTP proxying.

package_decisions.role: Credential placeholder parsing and substitution
package_decisions.reason: Proxy and policy evaluation share this one parse/substitution implementation, so keeping the internal package avoids duplicated security-sensitive parsing.
package_decisions.gate: Preserve total parsing and target variant validation.

package_decisions.role: HTTP proxy and CONNECT forwarding
package_decisions.reason: The proxy command is its sole production consumer; this private package owns the forward request lifecycle and delegates policy, identity and address checks to focused packages.
package_decisions.gate: Keep all admission checks before dialing.

package_decisions.role: Workload-facing EgressRules RPC
package_decisions.reason: The EgressRules service projects effective rules for an authenticated workload; it is separate from EgressAdmin and has distinct auth semantics.
package_decisions.gate: Preserve sandbox workload auth and admin isolation.

package_decisions.role: Destination classification and pinned resolution
package_decisions.reason: The proxy command and proxy implementation share address resolution/classification; the target is a security boundary with no unrelated caller.
package_decisions.gate: Keep checked addresses pinned through the dial.

package_decisions.role: Shared EgressCredential and egress-rule boundary models
package_decisions.reason: Policy Controller imports this package to reconcile EgressCredentials alongside proxy components; this is a real cross-component API and belongs with egress resource semantics.
package_decisions.gate: Do not move under the proxy or Policy Controller.

package_decisions.role: Sidecar executable and HTTP/gRPC/TLS relay runtime

package_decisions.gate: Move every production and test Go file as one boundary; keep cdk8s/Python settings and the published binary/image identity unchanged.

package_decisions.role: Experimental Iron Proxy comparison tests
package_decisions.reason: This x/ package contains only experiment tests and is explicitly outside the stable API; the parent bridge package is the only production implementation in this experiment.
package_decisions.gate: Retain only as experimental x/ coverage; do not expose it as a supported proxy.

package_decisions.role: Experimental Iron Proxy bridge
package_decisions.reason: The code and tests are explicitly under x/ and exercise a candidate transport bridge; there are no production imports or deployed callers.
